# Story 88 — Stale-write refusal speaks with one voice on the queue row (Story: CRM-95)

## Prerequisites

- **TICKETS-13-API (CRM-94)** must ship first. That story owns the 409 refusal (`REVISION_MISMATCH`) and the returning of the fresh revision on a successful write. This WEB story only unifies the on-screen behaviour of the three queue-row controls that already handle the refusal.
- Familiarity with the existing per-control 409 branches on the queue row (already shipped alongside `ticketAssign`, `ticketStatus`, `ticketCategory`).

---

## Story Goal

The three queue-row controls that write (`ticketAssign`, `ticketStatus`, `ticketCategory`) already detect a 409 `REVISION_MISMATCH` and show their own `staleTitle`. Today each control uses a slightly different sentence — two say “This ticket changed while you were looking at it”, one says “…while you were reading it”, and Arabic has a matching split. Three sentences for one cause teach a user that there are three causes. The story is to reduce these three strings to **one shared string per language**, keep the same recovery action across all three controls, and make sure the row picks up the fresh revision from a successful write so an agent’s second edit on the same row is not refused by their own first.

**Out of scope**

- Any `api/` change — CRM-94 owns the rule and the refusal.
- A fourth control. The queue row keeps the three controls it has.
- Any change to controls **off** the queue row (thread reply, ticket detail page). This story is scoped to `TicketQueuePage.tsx`.

## Product rules (from story)

- **BR-5** (owned upstream by CRM-94): a write carries the revision it read; the API returns 409 on mismatch.
- **BR-6**: every user-visible string comes from a resource file, in both languages.

**Current behaviour**

- Each of the three controls has its own `staleTitle` (and companion strings). Two English sentences vs one; two Arabic sentences vs one. The recovery affordance offered is `window.location.reload()`.

**New behaviour**

- One shared stale-refusal string per language, used by all three controls.
- One shared recovery affordance across all three controls (keep `window.location.reload()` — see task 3 below).
- After a successful write, the row carries the new revision returned by the API so a second write on the same row is not refused by the first.
- The 409 refusal is presented as an **informational** state (“somebody else got there first, take another look”), **not** an error. It must not be routed through the generic error banner.

## Frontend Tasks

### 1 — Introduce one shared stale-refusal string set

**File:** `web/src/shared/i18n/en.ts`

- Add a new namespace, e.g. `ticketStaleWrite`, next to the existing ticket-write namespaces:
  ```ts
  ticketStaleWrite: {
    title: 'This ticket changed while you were looking at it',
    body:  'Nothing went wrong — somebody else got there first. Take another look.',
    action:'Look again',
  },
  ```
  Exact wording is the planner’s suggestion; match the tone of the existing `ticketAssign.staleTitle` (line 276) and align with the acceptance-criterion phrasing “the ticket changed while it was being read and offers to look again”.
- Remove `staleTitle` (and any sibling `staleBody` / `staleAction`) from `ticketAssign` (line 276 region), `ticketStatus` (line 342 region), `ticketCategory` (line 356 region).

**File:** `web/src/shared/i18n/ar.ts`

- Add the mirrored `ticketStaleWrite` block. Use one Arabic sentence — collapse the two current variants at **lines 230, 292, 306**. Suggested:
  ```ts
  ticketStaleWrite: {
    title: 'تغيّرت هذه التذكرة أثناء نظرك إليها',
    body:  'لم يحدث خطأ — سبقك شخصٌ آخر. انظر مرة أخرى.',
    action:'انظر مرة أخرى',
  },
  ```
- Delete the three per-control stale strings at lines 230, 292, 306.

Both files must remain in lockstep so `parity.test.ts` and `scripts/verify-i18n-parity.mjs` pass.

### 2 — Point all three queue-row controls at the shared string

**File:** `web/src/pages/tickets/TicketQueuePage.tsx`

- Extract the per-control stale JSX into a single small internal component or helper (e.g. `renderStaleRefusal(t)` or `<StaleRefusal />`) so the three branches at **lines 186–195**, **236–…**, and **305–…** render the same title, body, and action from `t.ticketStaleWrite`.
- Replace:
  - `title={t.ticketAssign.staleTitle}` at **line 190**
  - `title={t.ticketCategory.staleTitle}` at **line 236**
  - `title={t.ticketStatus.staleTitle}` at **line 305**
  with the shared component / shared key `t.ticketStaleWrite.title`.
- The action button (currently `window.location.reload()`) is kept and centralised. See task 3.
- Do **not** change the `stale` predicate at **line 109** — it stays a check on `assign.error?.code === 'REVISION_MISMATCH'`, and the equivalent for the other two mutations. Preserve the guard at **line 197** (`assign.status === 'error' && !stale && assign.error`) so the generic error banner still hides when the refusal is a 409.

### 3 — Keep one recovery action across all three controls

The story is explicit: “if `window.location.reload()` is kept, keep it everywhere; if it is replaced, replace it everywhere.”

- Keep `window.location.reload()` for this story — replacing it is a larger UX change outside the point count. Route all three controls’ action button through the same handler in the shared component from task 2.
- Do **not** silently swap in a targeted refetch here; if the team later chooses a softer refresh, that is a separate story so all three controls move together.

### 4 — Preserve fresh-revision propagation on success

**Files:** `web/src/pages/tickets/useTicketQueue.ts`, `useAssignTicket.ts`, `useChangeCategory.ts`, `useChangeStatus.ts`.

- Read each hook and confirm the success handler writes the API response (including `revision`) back onto the queue row it mutated. If any of the three drops the revision on the floor (returns before merging, or merges only some fields), fix it so all three merge the returned row — key at minimum `id`, `revision`, `status`, `assigneeId`, `categoryId`, `updatedAt`. The comment at **TicketQueuePage.tsx line 343** already flags that a row can go stale relative to itself; make sure the three success paths obey the same merge shape.
- No new state shape. This is a consistency task: three success paths, one merge.

### 5 — Do not treat a 409 as a failure surface

**File:** `web/src/pages/tickets/TicketQueuePage.tsx`

- Confirm each of the three controls filters the 409 out of the generic error banner (assign already does at **line 197**). Apply the same `!stale` guard to the category and status branches if they lack it.
- The shared `<StaleRefusal />` renders inside the row (as today), not as a toast or a red banner. Visually neutral, not red — reuse the same styling `ticketAssign` uses today.

---

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Two controls on the same row race.** Agent hits Assign, it succeeds and updates the row’s revision (task 4). They then hit Change Status. Expected: the second write carries the fresh revision and is **not** refused. Enforced by task 4 merges in the three hooks.
- **409 raced with a plain 500.** Only `REVISION_MISMATCH` shows the stale refusal; any other error still uses the generic error branch — the `!stale` guard at **TicketQueuePage.tsx line 197** must apply to all three controls.
- **User in Arabic locale.** The Arabic `ticketStaleWrite` must be the exact wording used everywhere. `parity.test.ts` catches a missing key; `no-mirrored-styles.test.ts` catches accidental LTR wrapping.
- **Hardcoded fallback string.** If any refactor introduces a bare English string (`'Refused: stale'` or similar), `web/src/pages/no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts` will fail. Route every user-visible word through `t.ticketStaleWrite.*`.
- **Third party mutates row while the reload button is being clicked.** Reload always re-reads the queue; second stale is fine and shows the same string.
- **Old i18n keys still referenced somewhere.** After removing `ticketAssign.staleTitle`, `ticketStatus.staleTitle`, `ticketCategory.staleTitle`, grep the whole `web/` tree for each removed key — every hit must be updated or removed. Leaving one stale reference will break TypeScript typing on the `t` namespace when it is typed, or fail a test at runtime.
- **New control added later.** The shared `<StaleRefusal />` keeps the promise: adding a fourth control means importing the same component and the same handler.

## Migration / Rollback

- No schema change. No API change.
- Half-applied state (only some controls switched to the shared key): parity test still passes, but tests 1–3 fail loudly. Rollback is a plain revert of the two `i18n` files and `TicketQueuePage.tsx`.

## Verification Steps

1. **Frontend tests:** `cd web && npm test` — expect the three updated control tests and the new shared-behaviour test to pass, plus `parity.test.ts` and `no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts`.
2. **Frontend build:** `cd web && npm run build` — runs `tsc -b && vite build`; catches any dangling reference to a removed i18n key.
3. **i18n parity script:** `node scripts/verify-i18n-parity.mjs` from repo root.
4. **Regression — API untouched:** `cd api && npm test` — no failures. Confirms this WEB story did not drift into API code.
5. **Regression — no AI attribution:** from repo root, `grep -RniE 'copilot|chatgpt|claude|assistant|ai[- ]generated|ai[- ]assist' web/src` returns nothing new introduced by this change.
6. **Manual smoke (optional):** run `cd web && npm run dev`, open two tabs on the queue as different agents, edit the same ticket from one, then hit Assign / Change Status / Change Category from the other — each shows **the same title and body** and the same “look again” affordance.

## Done Criteria

- [x] All three writing controls on the queue row say one sentence for one cause, with one way out.
- [x] It is not reported as a failure — nothing failed and nothing was lost.
- [x] Only one copy shows at a time: one row, one ticket, one thing that happened to it.
- [x] The row already carries the fresh revision from a successful write; each control's own test pins it.
- [x] Both languages (BR-6). `cd web && npm test` (315), `npm run build`, and the six checks green.
- [x] No `api/` file touched.
- [x] No commit, doc or ignore-file entry mentions AI assistance.

**One string was not enough.** The plan asked for the three strings to become
one, which is right and not sufficient: the three copies of the markup around
them are how they drifted in the first place — two saying "looking at it", one
"reading it", and the category control borrowing the assign control's button
label because nobody had given it one. A shared string with three copies of the
block around it is the same drift one commit later. So the block is a component
and the strings moved with it.

**The strongest test here reads the resource file, not the screen.** Every
other test drives a control and compares what appears, which is the right way
round — but two keys with identical English would pass all of them and drift
the first time somebody edited one. So one test asserts that no `staleTitle`
key exists anywhere and that `reload` exists only under `ticketStale`. A
mutation adding a second sentence back fails it, and fails nothing else.

Three mutations run: a second sentence creeping back into the resource file
fails 1, reporting the refusal as a failure fails 6, and offering no way out
fails 3.

**STOP HERE. Report to the user and wait for confirmation before proceeding to the next story.**
